Front:
You committed a note locally, but your branch on GitHub has not changed. What normally sends the commit to GitHub?

A. git fetch
B. git push
C. git status
D. git add

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: B. git push

A. git fetch: Fetch downloads remote information.
B. git push: Push sends local commits to the remote.
C. git status: Status reports local state.
D. git add: Add selects content for a commit.

Key idea: Commit is local; push shares commits.
Source: https://git-scm.com/docs/git

Front:
You want to download remote history before deciding how to integrate it. Which command fits?

A. git pull
B. git commit
C. git fetch
D. git init

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: C. git fetch

A. git pull: Pull also integrates according to its options.
B. git commit: Commit records staged work.
C. git fetch: Fetch downloads remote history without merging it into your checked-out branch.
D. git init: Init creates a local repository.

Key idea: Fetch lets you inspect before integration.
Source: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-pull

Front:
Which statement correctly distinguishes Git from GitHub?

A. Git tracks versions; GitHub hosts repositories and collaboration tools.
B. Git requires GitHub for every commit.
C. GitHub is the name of the Git staging area.
D. Git and GitHub are interchangeable names.

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: A. Git tracks versions; GitHub hosts repositories and collaboration tools.

A. Git tracks versions; GitHub hosts repositories and collaboration tools.: Git works locally and GitHub adds hosted collaboration.
B. Git requires GitHub for every commit.: A local commit does not require GitHub.
C. GitHub is the name of the Git staging area.: The staging area belongs to Git.
D. Git and GitHub are interchangeable names.: They are different tools with connected uses.

Key idea: Local version control can exist without a hosting account.
Source: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/sourcecontrol/overview

Front:
A new reader needs setup instructions for this project. Which file is the best starting point?

A. CODEOWNERS
B. LICENSE
C. SECURITY.md
D. README.md

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: D. README.md

A. CODEOWNERS: CODEOWNERS maps paths to owners.
B. LICENSE: LICENSE describes reuse terms.
C. SECURITY.md: SECURITY describes reporting security concerns.
D. README.md: README introduces the project and explains how to use it.

Key idea: README is the project entry point.
Source: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-readmes

Front:
Which file identifies people or teams responsible for particular repository paths?

A. CODEOWNERS
B. README.md
C. A local stash
D. A Project view

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: A. CODEOWNERS

A. CODEOWNERS: CODEOWNERS maps file patterns to owners.
B. README.md: README describes the project.
C. A local stash: A stash holds temporary local work.
D. A Project view: A Project view organizes tracked items.

Key idea: Ownership mapping is separate from review enforcement.
Source: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners

Front:
A repository is public and has no license file. Which conclusion is appropriate?

A. All uses are automatically permitted.
B. Its reuse permissions need to be checked; public visibility is not an open-source license.
C. Starring it gives you a commercial license.
D. Forking removes all copyright restrictions.

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: B. Its reuse permissions need to be checked; public visibility is not an open-source license.

A. All uses are automatically permitted.: Visibility alone does not grant unrestricted reuse.
B. Its reuse permissions need to be checked; public visibility is not an open-source license.: Public access and licensing answer different questions.
C. Starring it gives you a commercial license.: A star does not grant licensing rights.
D. Forking removes all copyright restrictions.: A fork does not erase the original terms or rights.

Key idea: Visibility is not a license.
Source: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/licensing-a-repository

Front:
You want maintainers to review a branch change before integrating it. What should you open?

A. A secret gist
B. A milestone
C. A pull request
D. A star

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: C. A pull request

A. A secret gist: A gist shares a snippet.
B. A milestone: A milestone groups work.
C. A pull request: A PR proposes a change for discussion and review.
D. A star: A star saves or signals interest in a repository.

Key idea: A PR is a proposal to integrate a change.
Source: https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-github/github-flow

Front:
A PR description says Closes #12. Under the normal keyword behavior, when does the referenced issue close?

A. When you stage a file
B. When the PR is merged into the default branch
C. When someone stars the repository
D. When a branch is cloned

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: B. When the PR is merged into the default branch

A. When you stage a file: Staging is local Git work.
B. When the PR is merged into the default branch: The default-branch merge triggers the closing relationship.
C. When someone stars the repository: Stars do not close linked issues.
D. When a branch is cloned: Cloning does not trigger issue closure.

Key idea: Link the issue and merge to the correct branch.
Source: https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue

Front:
You need a simple static documentation website from repository content. Which feature fits?

A. Git stash
B. A team role
C. GitHub Mobile notifications
D. GitHub Pages

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: D. GitHub Pages

A. Git stash: Stash stores local work.
B. A team role: Roles govern access.
C. GitHub Mobile notifications: Notifications communicate activity.
D. GitHub Pages: Pages hosts static site content.

Key idea: Pages publishes a static site.
Source: https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/what-is-github-pages

Front:
You need a hosted development environment with a terminal to execute tests. Which option fits?

A. A Project board
B. A secret gist

D. A repository star

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: C. GitHub Codespaces

A. A Project board: A board tracks work.
B. A secret gist: A gist stores snippets.
C. GitHub Codespaces: Codespaces supplies a hosted development environment with compute.

Front:
In an Actions workflow, what is a runner?

A. The machine that executes a job
B. The title of a pull request
C. A repository license
D. The person who starred a repository

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: A. The machine that executes a job

A. The machine that executes a job: A runner provides the execution environment for a job.
B. The title of a pull request: A PR title is metadata.
C. A repository license: A license describes reuse terms.
D. The person who starred a repository: Starring does not define a runner.

Front:
Copilot suggests a fix and generated tests. What is the best next step?

A. Merge because AI generated it
B. Delete existing tests
C. Assume the tests ran in chat
D. Review the changes and run appropriate tests

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: D. Review the changes and run appropriate tests

A. Merge because AI generated it: Generated code can be incorrect.
B. Delete existing tests: Existing tests may catch regressions.
C. Assume the tests ran in chat: Generating test text is not proof of execution.
D. Review the changes and run appropriate tests: Review and execution provide evidence about the proposal.

Key idea: AI suggestions still need verification.
Source: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot

Front:
You want to see the same Project items in columns and in rows. What should you use?

A. Separate repositories for each layout
B. Board and table views of the same Project
C. Two forks
D. Two LICENSE files

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: B. Board and table views of the same Project

A. Separate repositories for each layout: Repositories are not needed to change a Project layout.
B. Board and table views of the same Project: Views present the same items in different layouts.
C. Two forks: Forks copy repositories, not layout settings.
D. Two LICENSE files: License files do not control views.

Key idea: A view changes presentation, not the underlying work.
Source: https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/learning-about-projects/about-projects

Front:
Your issue closed but its board item stayed In Progress. What should you check first?

A. Whether Git is installed locally
B. The commit author font
C. The Project workflow that updates Status on issue closure
D. The number of stars

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: C. The Project workflow that updates Status on issue closure

A. Whether Git is installed locally: Local Git installation does not set this Project automation.
B. The commit author font: Font is unrelated.
C. The Project workflow that updates Status on issue closure: The workflow controls the intended status update.
D. The number of stars: Stars do not drive this workflow.

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project

Front:
What is the main purpose of a GitHub Project?

A. Plan and track work using issues, PRs, and fields
B. Replace the Git commit history
C. Store passwords for every member
D. Provide a Python interpreter

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: A. Plan and track work using issues, PRs, and fields

A. Plan and track work using issues, PRs, and fields: Projects organize and visualize work.
B. Replace the Git commit history: Git history remains in the repository.
C. Store passwords for every member: Projects are not a password vault.
D. Provide a Python interpreter: A Project does not provide code execution.

Key idea: Planning tools organize work; they do not replace version control.
Source: https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/learning-about-projects/about-projects

Front:
A contributor needs to organize issues and PRs without pushing code. Which common repository role fits?

A. Admin
B. Write
C. Triage
D. Organization owner

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: C. Triage

A. Admin: Admin is broader than the stated task.
B. Write: Write includes code contribution capabilities beyond this need.
C. Triage: Triage supports issue and PR management without code write access.
D. Organization owner: Organization ownership is much broader.

Key idea: Match access to the task.
Source: https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-user-access-to-your-organizations-repositories/managing-repository-roles/repository-roles-for-an-organization

Front:
What makes an organization team different from a personal repository collaborator?

A. Teams can only contain outside collaborators.
B. Teams group organization members and can receive repository access together.
C. Teams automatically make every repository public.
D. A Project board creates organization membership.

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: B. Teams group organization members and can receive repository access together.

A. Teams can only contain outside collaborators.: Outside collaborators cannot belong to organization teams.
B. Teams group organization members and can receive repository access together.: Teams provide group-based organization access.
C. Teams automatically make every repository public.: A team does not automatically change repository visibility.
D. A Project board creates organization membership.: Project tracking does not create organization membership.

Key idea: Team membership belongs to an organization.
Source: https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/organizing-members-into-teams/about-teams

Front:
Who can read a secret gist if its URL is shared with them?

A. Only the author under all circumstances
B. Only enterprise owners
C. Only users with write access to a separate repository
D. Anyone who obtains the URL

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: D. Anyone who obtains the URL

A. Only the author under all circumstances: Secret gists are not private.
B. Only enterprise owners: Enterprise ownership is not required.
C. Only users with write access to a separate repository: A separate repository role is not the access condition.
D. Anyone who obtains the URL: The URL can expose an unlisted gist to others.

Key idea: Unlisted does not mean access-controlled.
Source: https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/editing-and-sharing-content-with-gists/creating-gists

Front:
You want to contribute to a project where you cannot push branches. Which route fits?

A. Fork, make a branch change, and propose a PR
B. Ask everyone for their password
C. Change the upstream visibility
D. Star the project to receive write access

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: A. Fork, make a branch change, and propose a PR

A. Fork, make a branch change, and propose a PR: A fork supports proposing a contribution without upstream write access.
B. Ask everyone for their password: Sharing passwords is not a contribution workflow.
C. Change the upstream visibility: Visibility is not yours to change and does not grant write access.
D. Star the project to receive write access: Stars do not grant permissions.

Key idea: A fork lets you prepare a contribution under your own account.
Source: https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/exploring-projects-on-github/contributing-to-open-source

Front:
Where can you discover reusable Actions and GitHub apps?

A. Only in a local stash
B. Only in CODEOWNERS
C. GitHub Marketplace
D. Only in a private gist

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: C. GitHub Marketplace

A. Only in a local stash: A stash holds local changes.
B. Only in CODEOWNERS: CODEOWNERS lists ownership.
C. GitHub Marketplace: Marketplace lists Actions and apps.
D. Only in a private gist: A gist is not the product catalog.

Key idea: Marketplace helps discover integrations.
Source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/get-started/actions-vs-apps

Front:
Before submitting a first contribution, what should you inspect?

A. Only the star count
B. The project contribution guidance and relevant issue context
C. Another contributor’s credentials
D. Only your own profile

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?
Back:
Correct: B. The project contribution guidance and relevant issue context

A. Only the star count: Popularity does not explain contribution expectations.
B. The project contribution guidance and relevant issue context: Guidance and issue context help you propose useful work.
C. Another contributor’s credentials: Credentials are unnecessary and private.
D. Only your own profile: Your profile does not explain project requirements.

Front:
Which Markdown syntax displays git status as inline code?

A. # git status
B. `git status`
C. - [ ] git status
D. > git status

Think: Which task does the question ask you to accomplish?

Correct: B. `git status`

B. `git status`: Backticks mark inline code.
C. - [ ] git status: This creates a task-list item.

Front:
You wrote - [ ] Try git fetch in an issue. What does it create?

Front:
How does a template-generated repository differ from a fork?

A. Only forks can contain Markdown.

D. A fork cannot receive pull requests.

A. Only forks can contain Markdown.: Both can contain Markdown.
B. Templates always grant upstream write access.: Templates do not grant upstream access.
C. A template-generated repository starts with a single commit; a fork retains upstream history.: Their history and intended relationship differ.

Front:
Which issue-search query finds open issues assigned to your signed-in account?

A. is:pr is:merged

You need updates from one issue conversation without all repository activity. What fits?

An AI response contains test code but no execution result. What has been demonstrated?

Which description best distinguishes agentic assistance from a single code suggestion?
